top_choice_rationale: P001 gives a single-part prize to Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock. It is one distinct idea (magic-wavelength trapping), demonstrated and then reproduced across national laboratories at the 10^-18 level, with downstream physics results (gravitational redshift over millimetre scales, bounds on drifting constants and ultralight dark matter) and a clean two-name allocation that no member contests. The citation must stay confined to the lattice clock to avoid the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 ranks second: the physics is a more surprising new state of matter with a theory-experiment chain, but omitting Bernevig and Hughes leaves a visible credit gap. P000 is last because a mature, defensible prize exists.
